summary: These four unit tests check the RobotPet.charge method by setting the battery to a known value, charging it, and asserting the new level. Together they cover normal charging, the 100 percent ceiling, draining with a negative amount, and the zero floor.

lines.text: Each test method lives inside the TestCase class and its name starts with test_, which is how unittest finds and runs it automatically.
Setting the battery directly gives the test a known starting point, so the result does not depend on whatever value the constructor chose.
This is the action under test: everything before it is setup and everything after it is checking the outcome.
The assertion compares the state after the call with the value you worked out by hand; if charge misbehaves, the test fails here with both numbers shown.
A second test for the same method, because one test per behaviour keeps failures easy to diagnose.
Charging 90 by 50 would give 140, so this deliberately pushes past the maximum to see whether the cap is applied.
The expected value is the ceiling rather than the raw sum, which is the rule this test exists to protect.
Passing a negative amount is the documented way to drain the battery, so it deserves its own test.
This is the mirror image of the cap test: draining 10 by 50 must stop at zero instead of going negative.
Testing both edges of the allowed range, 0 and 100, is a habit worth keeping for any value that is clamped.
